intro: A Portland band built on drums and vibes.
story: 1939 Ensemble is a Portland band often called post-rock, with drums and vibes at its center. They played Pickathon in 2017, and the Beats & Saints EP followed on Jealous Butcher in January 2018, with a release show at Mississippi Studios on January 12. Founding drummer José Medeles is still on Portland stages, and in October 2026 he performed in the stage production The Foggy Dew.
artist_reel_line: Drummer José Medeles took part in The Foggy Dew on a Portland stage in 2026.

story: Anna Roberts-Gevalt, from Vermont, and Elizabeth LaPrelle, from rural Virginia and known as one of the finest traditional singers of her generation, sing Appalachian ballads in close harmony. Their self-titled 2015 album was a favorite of A Green Man Review, and they played Pickathon in 2017. The Invisible Comes to Us, in March 2018, was their Smithsonian Folkways debut, and PopMatters called it enchantingly experimental. It closed their run as a duo, and each has since turned to separate projects.
artist_reel_line: The Invisible Comes to Us, their 2018 Folkways album, closed their run as a duo.

story: Huun-Huur-Tu began in 1992 as Kunggurtug, a Tuvan throat-singing group, and the name means sun propeller, or sunbeams. They were among the first Tuvan folk groups to tour the world, and they have worked with Frank Zappa, the Kronos Quartet, The Chieftains and the Moscow Art Trio. They played Pickathon in 2017. In April 2024 they released an album with Carmen Rizzo and Dhani Harrison, and in late 2026 they toured Europe, still under the name that means sunbeams.
artist_reel_line: In 2024 they made an album with Carmen Rizzo and Dhani Harrison, then toured Europe.

story: Kaia Kater is a Montreal-born, Grenadian-Canadian banjo player who studied Appalachian music in West Virginia. Nine Pin, produced by Chris Bartos and recorded in a single day in Toronto, came out in 2016, and The Guardian's Neil Spencer heard bluegrass meeting Nina Simone. She played Pickathon in 2017. Grenades, in October 2018, earned a Juno nomination and a Polaris long-list spot, and Strange Medicine, from 2024, was a 2025 Juno nominee for Contemporary Roots Album. A deluxe edition followed in September 2026.
artist_reel_line: Strange Medicine, a 2025 Juno nominee, got a deluxe edition in September 2026.

story: Pinegrove formed in Montclair, New Jersey, in 2010 around the singer-songwriter Evan Stephens Hall and the drummer Zack Levine, who have played together since childhood. Cardinal, recorded in the band's parents' basements, came out February 12, 2016 on Run for Cover and appeared on many national year-end lists. They played Pickathon in 2017. Skylight followed in 2018, Marigold in 2020 and 11:11 in 2022, and in November 2026 Hall and Levine announced a return to the stage in 2027.
artist_reel_line: In November 2026 they announced a 2027 return to live shows.

story: Hiss Golden Messenger is M.C. Taylor's band. Heart Like a Levee in 2016 and Hallelujah Anyhow in 2017 both came out on Merge, and reviewers heard the second as close to the band's live sound. They played Pickathon in 2014, 2015 and 2017. Terms of Surrender, produced by Taylor and Brad Cook, followed September 20, 2019, and The Guardian's Michael Hann heard songs of despair turned to hope; it was nominated for the Grammy for Best Americana Album. Quietly Blowing It came in 2021 and I'm People, with guests including Sam Beam, on Chrysalis in 2026.
artist_reel_line: I'm People came out on Chrysalis in 2026, with guests including Sam Beam.

intro: The Modern Lovers' founder, on his own.
story: Jonathan Richman counts 1976's Jonathan Richman and the Modern Lovers, made with a new band, as his real debut. The earlier sessions, released as The Modern Lovers the same year, appear on Rolling Stone's 500 greatest albums list, at No. 381 in 2003 and No. 288 in 2020. From 1976 to 1988 he billed his backing bands as the Modern Lovers before going solo, with Back in Your Life in 1979. He played Pickathon in 2014 and 2017. Only Frozen Sky Anyway came out on Blue Arrow in 2025.
artist_reel_line: Only Frozen Sky Anyway came out on Blue Arrow in 2025.

story: Luke Bell was raised in Wyoming in a family of homesteaders, worked as a ranch hand and studied agroecology before moving to Austin, New Orleans and Nashville. He told Rolling Stone he grew up on Nirvana and punk but was drawn to the simplicity and timelessness of honky-tonk. His self-titled album came out June 17, 2016 on Bill Hill Records, recorded in Nashville with the producer Andrija Tokic, and Mojo called it wonderfully 50 years out of date. He played Pickathon in 2017 and was named Best Male Honky Tonk Artist at the 2018 Ameripolitan Awards. He died in August 2022. The King Is Back, a posthumous record, came out in 2025.
artist_reel_line: The King Is Back, a posthumous record, came out in 2025.

story: Chad Ubovich started as a bassist, then guitarist, in Mikal Cronin's band and toured with Ty Segall around Goodbye Bread in 2011 before building Meatbodies, first billed as Chad and the Meatbodies. The self-titled debut came in 2014, and Alice came out February 10, 2017 on In the Red. Meatbodies played Pickathon in 2015 and 2017, and Ubovich also wrote for and toured with Fuzz, Segall's band. Flora Ocean Tiger Bloom, after years in the making, came out in 2024, and they came back to Pickathon in 2026.
artist_reel_line: Flora Ocean Tiger Bloom, a long-gestating album, came out in 2024.

story: Tim Darcy was born in Arizona and made his way through Colorado and New Hampshire to Montreal, where he met the rest of Ought and became its singer. His first solo album, Saturday Night, came out February 17, 2017 on Jagjaguwar, recorded on nights and weekends in a studio storeroom while Ought made Sun Coming Down, and NPR praised its first single as soul-searching Americana. He played Pickathon that year. Ought split quietly in 2021, and Darcy now plays in Cola, a Montreal post-punk band formed with the former Ought member Ben Stidworthy.
artist_reel_line: Cola, with Ben Stidworthy from Ought, is now his main band.
